# Børne-Unge Psyk. Afd. 40

Børne-Unge Psyk. Afd. 40 is a child and adolescent psychiatry department (børne- og ungdomspsykiatrisk afdeling) reporting ADHD treatment data into the Danish national ADHD-databasen, a quality-monitoring registry that tracks how well psychiatric departments across Denmark meet standardized care indicators for ADHD assessment and treatment [^src1]. The department is listed as part of [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] [^src1] [^src4], appearing repeatedly in indicator tables under that region [^src2] [^src3].

In the 2023 annual report (covering the period 01.04.2023–31.03.2024), the department is recorded under the name "Børne-Unge Psyk. Afd. 40." It reported that 363 of 610 treatment courses (60%) included a somatic examination, one of the database's process indicators [^src1]. On another indicator table it is shown with a result of "9 / 40, 0 (0), 23 (11-38)" [^src2]. For Indikator 3 — diagnostic conferences held within 120 days of the start of assessment — the department achieved 31% fulfillment out of 610 assessment courses, a claim explicitly logged against [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] [^src3]. Elsewhere the department is shown scoring "187 / 610 ... 31 (27-34)" [^src3], "74 / 388, 0 (0), 19 (15-23)" [^src4], "165 / 388, 0 (0), 43 (38-48)" [^src5], and, in an appendix on refuted/discounted assessment courses, the figures "7 3 7" [^src6].

The 2024 annual report (covering 01.04.2024–31.03.2025) lists what appears to be the same unit under a slightly changed name, "Børne-Unge Psyk. Klinik 40.K," still reporting into the same national database. Under this name it recorded "219 / 690" with a 32% (28-35) fulfillment rate [^src7], "159 / 731" at 22% (19-25) [^src8], "95 / 497" at 19% (16-23) [^src9], "247 / 497" at 50% (45-54) [^src10], "279 / 497, 0 (0), 56 (52-61)" [^src10], and "10 / 15" at 67% (38-88) [^src11].

Across both reporting years, the department's figures sit within a national picture in which most quality indicators fall well short of the database's 90% development target, reflecting system-wide pressures such as staffing shortages, rising referral volumes, and registration inconsistencies affecting child and adolescent psychiatry departments across Denmark [^src1] [^src3] [^src4]. The database itself was expanded during this period to include adult psychiatry and private practice data, part of a broader national effort — including work by the Danish Multidisciplinary Psychiatry Groups — to standardize ADHD assessment guidelines [^src1].
